newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NetComm says Compaq okays merger.
newsitem.headline: NetComm says Compaq okays merger.

text.p: Modem maker NetComm Ltd said on Monday that U.S. computer giant Compaq Computer Corp, a minor shareholder in NetComm's merger partner Banksia Technologies Pty Ltd, supported the agreed merger between NetComm and Banksia.

"We have the full support from Compaq for the merger," Banksia managing director David Stewart told reporters. He will also be managing director of the enlarged NetComm and its largest single shareholder.
On Thursday, the two companies announced their proposed merger to create a group with A$70 million in sales.
Shareholders of Banksia -- Stewart, who owns 92.04 percent and Microcom Inc with 7.96 percent -- will be issued pro rata with shares in NetComm, representing 52 percent of the expanded share capital.
Microcom is wholly owned by Compaq Computers.

Stewart said Banksia has an exclusive agreement with Microcom to develop modems, to be called 'New Wave' for the U.S. computer giant to market internationally, with sales expected to start in 1997/98.
"We shall start to see some of that revenue stream in fiscal 1998," Stewart said.
He said the merged group also has a strategic agreement with U.S. communications and avionics equipment maker Rockwell International.
Stewart said he expected the merged group to be profitable in 1997/98 despite seeing an increased squeeze on margins.
He said profit would be underpinned by higher modem volume growth.

Investors have welcomed the merger, pushing NetComm shares up to a high of 90 cents after Thursday's merger announcement from 60 cents before the announcement, but have since retreated to below 70 cents.
At 1.10 p.m. (0310 GMT), NetComm shares were seven cents lower at 68 cents.
The merger is subject to the approval of NetComm shareholders and anti-monopolies watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
